The plunger part is where the cheap manufacturing shows: the wire mesh and spring are crude, compared to the Bodum. I can do 2.5 mph without affecting my productivity, easily racking up 10000 or more steps a day.  Combining the relatively inane task of hashing through email with the equally inane task of walking in place actually makes both activities worthwhile./ (I call this the stationery-stationary paradox.) text_fidelity_a: ENO, Eagles Nest Outfitters SingleNest Lightweight Camping Hammock, Emerald/Khaki Really good.  Consider this though: If you get a double nest there is more material that you can wrap yourself with. If you are trying to travel lighter, this one is better.  Remember if you are going to camp or backpack and you intend to sleep in a hammock, you need what's call a bottom quilt under your hammock.  A sleeping bag will just compress and your butt will freeze at night, even in summer.  the quilt is outside of your hammock so it maintains loft and warmth.  Do some research, figure out your proper hang height and distance, use a ridgeline, sleep at an angle, put a small pillow under your knee on your outstretched leg and or bend the other leg and you will sleep like a king. I once slept in an Eno double nest for two years straight and I miss it.  Hammock camping is the BEST, and I highly recommend it for grown ups who hate sleeping on the rocky ground.  Your entire outlook on the outdoors will change once you try hammock camping.  Go for it!

text_fidelity_a:
Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Columbia Crescent Peak 23L Backpack For a daypack, this is a great bag. Purchased from a Columbia outlet for under $30, but I'd be willing to spend up to $75 on this bag.

On the outside, there are a ton of straps on it, it might take you a little while to get it comfortable, but once you do, you won't notice it is there. The sternum strap has slides to sit comfortably on your chest. The shoulder straps are made of a foam/mesh combo. They can be a little rigid at first, but after a number of wearings mine have become comfortable. They also have two straps at the top, to adjust how the shoulder straps sit on you. The waist strap is the least comfortable, as it is just the nylon strap and a buckle, but it does a good job at taking some of the weight off of your shoulders. There are pullcords to strap things to, like hiking poles if you need to. The back is rigid, yet comfortable. I usually put water bottles in it, and in my older bag they would press against my back causing aches. This bag has a rigid back to stop whatever is in the bag from pressing against you, but then has comfortable padding to keep you going.

To the inside, there are three pockets, the main one, one for your phone, keys, etc, and the one on the front, which has two zippers. I use this for the sunblock, bugspray, all the frequently used things. The main compartment has a sleeve for a bladder though it does not come with one.

Storage wise, it is plenty for a day long adventure for one where the weather might change, or plenty of room for a few people when no clothing is needed. I've hiked 4+ hours with this bag, carrying food/drink for four people total. The straps took all the weight off of my shoulders. I've also had enough room to bike to work, with a full change of clothes and toiletries, and a water bottle.

I haven't had to use the rain-fly yet, but it will cover the entire pack when it is full.

The 'backdraft' is useless. You'll sweat just as much. The only benefit, is that once you do start sweating, it's mesh against padding, so it'll dry quickly.

All in all, I'd buy this bag again if it broke on me.
text_fidelity_b: Columbia Crescent Peak 23L Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps Once in a while a product comes along that looks like it might pose a solution to a different problem than what it is actually intended for. These Ringside Gel Wraps are obviously designed to protect your hands while either working out or sparring in the ring. But I ordered them for a different unrelated purpose -- protecting my knuckles while cutting/trimming trees in our wetlands. We live in Southwest Florida where the brush grows all year around and not only grows quickly but also tries to choke out its neighbors by fighting for the available sunlight and water. That makes for tight quarters and a lot of "barked" knuckles while maneuvering tools and changing positions.

There are pros and cons to how this product is constructed:

PROS
1. They fit your hands ergonomically without limiting your flexibility. I am actually typing this review with the gloves on.
2. The gel padding on the knuckles is positioned for proper protection and provides a feeling of confidence and security.
3. There is a stretchy strap just below the knuckles that helps keep the glove in position.
4. The glove fastens around your wrist with an adjustable velcro strap.
5. There is a second strap that fastens over the first one which holds the velcro strap in place and actually provides good wrist support.
6. The gloves are breathable and machine washable.
7. Last but not least, they come in several colors: blue, grey, pink, and red.

CONS
1. Even though I am a bigger guy, I have always worn a large size in every type of glove. Be warned that these gloves run small.
2. While the overall construction is quite good, the sewing around the cut-off fingers is not uniform. The point where the gloves are
cut off (on the inside of the hand) are folded under and stitched together -- at least that was the intention. However the stitching is
"balled up" in different parts and loose strings are evident in some of the fingers. That appears to be a quality control problem.
3. I am assuming that since the gloves are too small for me that the smaller size carries over to make the fingers too tight for comfort.
Perhaps that will loosen up with wear and washing.

So overall I think that this is a great product for what it is intended, but at 65 years old I'm not the guy to punch someone with them on or
to test them out in any manner that would hurt these old bones. At my age I'm trying to protect myself, not break my hands. The manufacturer might want to take a closer look at how the fingers are sewn together, but overall this is a good looking product that should serve its purpose quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps

Updated 8/8/16:

We recently bought another Bago lightweight foldable backpack - since our original purchases, Bago has made several changes to the original backpack in the form of an additional zip pocket on the front and deeper mesh side pockets. Having used these daypacks for a number of years now, they remain among my favorite! They are extraordinarily lightweight, and really store a lot. text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

text_fidelity_a: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size I'm always wary of buying air mattresses since I've never had one last more than a couple seasons before constantly deflating during the night. I hope this one is different, and so far after 4 nights it's performed beautifully. The mattress is very comfortable and I noticed that part of the reason for this is that the air chambers go from side to side instead of lengthwise like some other models. This seems to different zones for support and I'll look for this in any future air mattress purchases. I experienced very little initial stretching which the instructions say is common for the first few nights. I slept on it for 3 nights and only added a tiny bit of air the last night just to see how firm it would get. A nice touch is that the sides are slightly higher than the middle, which is very subtle but I'm sure keeps you from rolling off during the night. It comes with a good quality storage bag which sould help protect it when stored. The rechargable pump works well for inflating and deflating and comes with an AC adapter, car charger, and a couple different nozzles. Actually, the charger is the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars - for two reasons. First, it has NiCd batteries which are pretty old school in terms of rechargeables and won't last very long, at which point it becomes a brick. Ominously, perhaps they are only meant to last as long as the mattress? Second, the charger and accessories don't come with any kind of stuff sack or even a pocket in the mattress bag. I nice little cheapo storage sack for the charger and accessories is really needed. Other than that, so far so good. Very comfortable mattress.
text_fidelity_b: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size

So please take that into consideration in this review.

We each got a JOOLA paddle, slightly different, and like them both. We know nothing about the brand, we are not experts on what brands or elements of a paddle are best, but we are trying different ones. This JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle so far is very nice and I do like it. Mine is slightly heavier than hers, and I do notice the difference in weight, and as negligible as the difference really is, it is noticeable. We're actually surprised by how such a little amount can be felt. That said, I do not have an issue when swinging or hitting due to the "added weight." It feels like a smooth swing, a solid contact.

I think what I like most is the grip. I can FEEL the solid connection with the handle. From the moment we each first held ours, the number one thing we felt and noticed and were drawn to in each of our JOOLA paddles is the GRIP. This alone is likely going to make my JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle my go-to paddle. As we get better, it might change, but right now, I like that connection to the paddle.

In the end, I like this JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle and am very happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle - Carbon Surface with High Grit & Spin, Elongated Handle, USAPA Approved 2022 Ben Johns Paddle - Available with Pickle Ball Paddle Cover

VEVESMUNDO 50L Hiking Backpack Men Women for Travel Mountaineering Climbing Camping Trekking (Blue) I’ll admit, this is our first hiking backpack, but we are very pleased with the choice. It’s lightweight, but the materials feel solid enough for longevity. it’s comfortable on either of our backs. And it’s got plenty of room. We do a couple hours to half a day hikes/walks and wanted to be able to carry things we want (eating, comfort) as well as for safety (I’m putting together a safety kit). This backpack fits it all.

We’ve been using it just around some smaller area trails - not longer hiking yet - for some days out during Covid and it’s carried a lot of things. We have it filled right now from yesterday’s outing - it worked perfectly. There are plenty of spots/pockets/hooks for carrying in or attaching to. Adjusting the straps to fit each of our bodies was easy and quick.

For beginners or midlevel hikers and day trips just getting around, I think it’s perfect. I can’t speak to hiking pros, but I can’t (currently) see what more you’d need. This has quickly become a go-to for us. We have a day bag, but I see us filling this with extras, keeping it by the door, and grabbing it for a range of days out.

Love the colors (blue with orange) and the material. Love the way it sits. Even fully loaded we were both comfortable, so that was an added plus. We hope to one day get out for longer trips and think this will be a perfect backpack to take us safely into the wilds.

Overall we are very happy with this backpack and happy we chose it.

Weight of 175 lbs., Front and Rear Caliper Brakes, Rear Axle Pegs, 12-Inch Inflatable Wheels Definitely for a 7-11 year old. Assembly: Took 2 of us about an hour because of the terrible directions and lack of weird tools needed to tighten/loosen brakes. Just a PIA.

The pegs on the back wheel immediately injured my 8 year old cutting her ankle. FAIL. She is an awesome scooter connoisseur but this design just tears up your ankles. My 11 year old then tried and his sneaker got caught on the back pegs almost causing a wipeout but he ripped his sneaker free and recovered with a minor stumble. FAIL. We want to like this scooter but it is made for little kids with pretty poor balance that can not use a regular scooter. We will probably keep it for now--because it is great to ride over rocks and tough terrain with the awesome bike wheel on it.

Just beware that this may not fit your needs--or may--but know what you are buying before you attempt the annoying assembly.

text_fidelity_a:
Cleveland Golf Launcher UHX Utility Club Okay, I'm probably the odd ball out on this discussion. I've tried several hybrid styles, makes and models and struggled with consistency. Distance was also not what I was expecting, regardless of lie or contact. I even pulled the 3 wood (fairway metal) out of my bag for the same reason. I hit my driver very well, even drivers I haven't spent time with. So, I was left in a no win situation.

I started watching videos and found that the "utility clubs" were available and seemed to be very useable for the person who hits irons well. So, I made the gamble and bought this, relatively inexpensive, utility club to try. Well, it checked all my boxes. The 18* 3 iron gives me that hybrid/fairway wood distance without all the inconsistency. I hit it well and the ball flight is exactly what I expected it to be. So far I've played 3 rounds with it, hit it 2-3 times from the ground and 2-3 times off the tee (short par 4 doglegs) and virtually every shot has been spot on.

It's also forgiving. I've hit a few off the toe end without a large loss of yardage and no right fade. It just goes short and straight with the mishits.

If you hit your longer irons well and struggle with the hybrid/fairway woods, this is definitely worth a try.

FYI, I hit 5 or 6 shots in the backyard before taking it to the course. That's it!
text_fidelity_b: Cleveland Golf Launcher UHX Utility Club

Condition 1 30” Case, Hard Lockable Storage Box, Water Resistant Plastic Travel Case, Protective Luggage with Foam Insert, Rebel Economy, 2041, 30.63"x11.52"x3.56" "Any product is only as strong as its weakest part." And the weakest part of this case are the latches. Although I didn't want to prove it to myself and ruin this Condition 1 case, the light plastic used and flimsy design will not hold up to any hard use.

I know that this is considered an "Economy Grade Case", but I wouldn't trust it to protect any expensive firearms. Please remember that "water resistant" doesn't mean "water proof", it should protect your weapon from rain but it can not be submerged. Also remember that any weapon stored either in a hard or a soft case will eventually rust and/or discolor unless it is allowed to breathe and air out on occasion. It is amazing how badly a stored firearm can look after being kept in a humid environment for any length of time.

Dropping this case on a hard surface will eventually cause the case to fail if anything of any weight is placed within it. That of course is not what this case is designed for and you shouldn't accidently drop it from anything above shoulder height. While this might provide adequate protection for inexpensive weapons I am always surprised when a manufacturer tries to enter into the lowest end of the market when their standard products already have a good reputation.
text_fidelity_b: Condition 1 30” Case, Hard Lockable Storage Box, Water Resistant Plastic Travel Case, Protective Luggage with Foam Insert, Rebel Economy, 2041, 30.63"x11.52"x3.56"

Razor A5 Lux Kick Scooter for Kids Ages 8+ - 8" Urethane Wheels, Anodized Finish Featuring Bold Colors and Graphics, for Riders up to 220 lbs What I dislike?? I paid 67 last week now it is LESS....lol. But I will say it is worth the money. I am a 52 year old 5'10" adult and the last time I rode a Razor Brand kick scooter Harry Potter was in the theaters and I was "old" for scooters then. And had a very bad wreck due to the brake not really supporting my weight.
Rest assured ...I am under the 220 pound limit and the brake on this DOES work but not on a dime. Plan ahead.
The huge wheels make cracks and bumps easy. On smooth pavement it is a smooth ride....on rough pavement.....yep, rough ride. Will jar you pretty good. I use it for an 8 block radius. I have seen reviews of people who use it for much larger spans. I just WISH this product had existed when I was a teen or in my 20s. Also, if you meet a heel too steep to kick scoot, it is very easy to just pick it up or push it till you can easily go again. I think it weighs about 7 lbs. Don't quote me but that is something anyone can handle.

Here is what to know....as long as you an adult rider do not take this to a skate park, these days, no one is gonna laugh or poke fun. Scooters are hot now whether electric or kick and this scooter is great for people young or old. It is low to the ground, easy to kick, easy to ride, light weight...total fun.
I own the Razor E300. I wanted this for different reasons. It is 100 percent suitable for an adult human to ride. It IS a scooter and you could fall so wear your helmet. You already look a tad goofy....so don't worry what others think. Put that helmet to protect your brain and enjoy a fun ride!

Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black My use is for 1" diameter by 5" long tactical lights which do not protrude out the bottom. I also tried it with a 2 C cell light which protrudes out the bottom a lot.

I was looking for something either with a flap cover or a snug but easy to insert fit. This is neither. It has no cover flap, but has a VERY snug fit on this type of light. However it is made up of a series of internal flaps and elastic straps you have to guide the light through to get it into this case. You cannot easily do this one handed as you have to spread two internal flaps apart and hold them that way to insert the light. In addition if you have to sit/stand as in driving patrol or the like, the light works it's way out the top even if it doesn't protrude out the bottom. Since there is nothing to lock it in, the movement of sitting and moving around when seated pushes against the bottom squeezing the light upward like squeezing a toothpaste tube. Eventually it pops out the top. In addition if your light has a tailcap switch it will get turned on without your knowing it in daytime (you would see the light at night), draining the batteries, as there is nothing protecting the tailcap switch from being pressed against the seat bottom.

From my experience with it, this is pretty useless if you are going to be wearing it on a belt in the vertical position, whether a short small diameter or longer larger diameter light. As a temporary worklight holder it isn't bad, but how often do you need a worklight on your belt?
text_fidelity_b: Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black

text_fidelity_a: NeoSport Exclusive Mens and Women’s XSPAN Sock Available in 1.5MM or 5MM Parent I love these things. I have owned just about every kind of booty for trying to keep my feet warm.  I have bought just about 1 pair of everything out there, I think.  The only downside to these is they ARE neoprene, so if your feet sweat, your feet will be moist inside the booty/sock.  You will be wet, but they will stay warm, and your feet will stay warm, in my experience.  I put on a medium pair of wool-type socks, these socks over that, and then my insulated felt pack boots. Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

text_fidelity_a:
Forgan of St. Andrews 21 Golf Ball Pick Up Tube [Misc.] This is a fairly simple product and, as such, you would think it would be pretty difficult to screw up. The theory behind item's construction is sound, but the construction is lousy. Specifically, I will point you to the cap at the top of the tube; this cap is poorly fitted to the tube and readily falls off w/o much prompting. There are only two things keeping balls inside this tube, the plastic claw at the bottom of the tube and the top cap. If one of these fails, you're left with an open tube that balls can fall out of at their leisure, which is exactly what I experienced. The top cap repeatedly fell off of my tube during use, a couple times from tipping the tube to where the balls pressed against the cap and a couple times after leaving the tube in my car filled with balls. I've owned other ball tubes and have been able to carry them horizontally and man-handle them fairly roughly w/o ever having this issue. The end result of owning this product that was supposed to keep me from having to bend over to pick up golf balls was that I was bending over to pick up balls that had fallen out of the tube. Sweet sweet irony!

I thought I may have just received a defective product and requested a refund from Amazon and was content to leave it at that. However, one of my golfing buddies said he purchased this tube and experienced the same issue, which leads me to believe this product is just generally poorly made.
text_fidelity_b: Forgan of St. Andrews 21 Golf Ball Pick Up Tube [Misc.]

text_fidelity_a: OGIO Half Dome Duffel Bag I have a bunch of duffel bags (sometimes I think I collect them); my favorite is a standard Nike bag, but this one is better if you are looking for really high quality stuff; the main black fabric or material is very thick and heavy duty, I think it will last a very long time.  In addition the main zipper is the heaviest zipper I have seen in several years on ANYTHING.  It seems to hold a decent amount of stuff; one thing that lessens the ability to hold stuff is the design (that's probably why it is called half dome, duh); it's kind of rounded on the top (not the usual squarish or rectangular design of most duffel bags I have owned), so you lose a little room on the top side.  It also has a nice little pocket on the side for an ipod or iphone or whatever small electronic device you want to carry on the outside of your bag.  The main shoulder strap is adjustable and fairly comfortable--but it isn't padded and if you are carrying any fairly heavy things, it isn't comfortable to carry about using the shoulder strap.  It also has a nice fairly solid rectangular bottom piece that fits in the bottom of the bag that provides support for the bag.  One thing I thought almost all duffel bags had was more than one decent sized compartment, usually two zippers with their own sections.  This unit only has the one main compartment (and the  other  really small one for electronic stuff  which does have a small zipper (again, really heavy duty).  It's like a heavy duty jacket zipper.  In sum it is a well made piece of merchandise; it will last years even with some abuse.  One final thing, the main reason I bought this is for airplane trips where you take carry on; this will fit in any airline compartment, and it still holds a reasonable amount of stuff (well, for us men)(I know, chauvinist pig), so it works for me for this purpose.
text_fidelity_b: OGIO Half Dome Duffel Bag

MoiShow Kids Paddle Board Paddle, 3-Pieces SUP Paddle Adjustable Floating Youth Paddle with Durable High-Grade Aluminium Shaft & Updated PP Fiberglass Blade I love the stunning, bright burnt orange color of the paddle with off white contrasts on the handle and the length adjustment section. I chose this color because it is easy to spot in case it slips away from us.

The paddle part has an outward curve with a slight concave shape on the inside to allow ease when you put the paddle into the water and have a smooth start with stroking. The concave allows you to have more pressure on pushing water and get you moving faster.

I had two concerns about the lock bar.
1. When I opened it and adjusted the length, the lock bar wasn't tight enough. I could easily adjust the length and even slide the handle part out, which means I could lose the other end of the paddle. The way the lock bar is set up, it does not allow me to adjust the tiny in between screw to make it tighter. I took the risk to open the lock bar, and carefully forced it around clockwise 2 times, thankfully it did not snap the plastic and it is secure now (see image).
2. As mentioned, that section is plastic and with wear and tear, it will crack then you will not be able to adjust the length. When that happens, you will just need to drill and put in a screw to secure them together.

Suggestion for the company:
Since the poles are made of some kind of metal, why not make the lock bar area metal as well instead of plastic? Allow us to be able to adjust the screw for tightness will make this 5 stars.

This paddle is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on amazon.
text_fidelity_b: MoiShow Kids Paddle Board Paddle, 3-Pieces SUP Paddle Adjustable Floating Youth Paddle with Durable High-Grade Aluminium Shaft & Updated PP Fiberglass Blade
